prize_parts.citation: For the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation and the universality class of non-equilibrium interface growth it defines, and for its first clean experimental confirmation.

statement.case_for: KPZ is a single, compact stochastic equation that organises a very large body of non-equilibrium behaviour: its scaling exponents and Tracy-Widom-type fluctuation statistics are universal, and the same class appears in growth, directed polymers, random matrices, exclusion processes and integrable models. It is a case where the essential mechanism is understood, not merely observed. The theory dates from 1986, and the experimental confirmation of the predicted distributions (Takeuchi and Sano, 2010-2011) has been independently reproduced, so maturity is not in question. A theory-plus-experiment pair is also a configuration the prize has handled well. Statistical physics proper, as opposed to condensed matter and quantum optics, has few candidates on this list, and this one honours the field's conceptual core.
statement.case_against: My opening ballot was the only one on the shortlist that placed B056 anywhere, so I have to take seriously that colleagues do not see it as a leading candidate. The attribution is genuinely imperfect: Parisi, a co-author of the 1986 work, is outside the credited names and already has a prize, and the exact solutions (Johansson, Spohn, Sasamoto, Amir-Corwin-Quastel and others) that turned KPZ into a precise mathematical theory are not credited, so Kardar, Zhang and Takeuchi would honour the equation and the experiment rather than the most rigorous part of the story. The practical benefit is also indirect, and some colleagues will weigh that against candidates with a clear instrument or technological payoff.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks topological insulators first because Kane and Mele's prediction and Molenkamp's HgTe observation form a clean example of theory and experiment jointly revealing a new phase, confirmed in many platforms and arguably overdue.
responses.response: I agree on the physics, and B015 is my second choice for the same reason. Where I qualify his view is attribution and sequence: as he notes himself, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe proposal and the 3D work of Fu, Kane, Moore, Hasan, Hsieh and Cava sit outside or at the edge of the credited trio, and Zhang is deceased, so the trio is harder to defend than a theory-plus-experiment label suggests. The 2016 prize on topological phases also covered some of the conceptual ground. I would not rule B015 out, but I do not find it more cleanly attributable than KPZ, and conceptual importance alone does not put it clearly ahead.

responses.point: Olsson ranks magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first: an original 2018 experiment with a clear 2011 theoretical precursor, widely reproduced, launching a large field.
responses.response: The Bistritzer-MacDonald model is a transparent mechanism and I ranked B038 third for that reason. My reservation is one she partly shares: the origin of the superconductivity is unresolved, the field is only eight years old and moving fast, and the first author Cao and earlier twistronics work (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell) are not in the credited names. I would rather wait until a mechanism is established than reward the platform before its central question is answered. If the committee does go for moire materials now, the theory-plus-experiment trio is defensible.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks first as a measurement instrument that changed what can be measured, reaching 1e-18, reproduced by many laboratories, with a clean two-person credit.
responses.response: On maturity and attribution B002 is the best-credited candidate on the list, and I put it on my own ballot, though low. My concern is not rigour but conceptual novelty: the committee has already recognised the frequency comb (2005) and ion-trap control (2012), and Ye was part of the comb story. A prize for ever better accuracy rewards a superb technique, but I find it less compelling than a mechanism-level result such as KPZ. I would accept it if the committee decides clean attribution should dominate, but that is a criterion of safety rather than of discovery.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks the experimental Higgs discovery first as the clearest discovery of a generation, extremely mature, while accepting that credit in ATLAS and CMS is diffuse.
responses.response: I do not dispute the scientific significance. My difficulty is the one Olsson raises in her own ballot: the three credited names are founding spokespersons and project leaders, not individuals who made the decisive measurement, so any selection from collaborations of thousands is a statement about leadership rather than discovery. Of the leading candidates, this is the weakest fit with the statutes' requirement to name those who made the discovery. I would need a clear argument for why these three and not accelerator or analysis leaders before I could support B053.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a configuration that omits Parisi and the exact-solution contributors (Johansson, Spohn, Sasamoto, Amir-Corwin-Quastel); the supplied credited names do not allow them.
Whether Takeuchi's liquid-crystal experiments should count as the decisive experimental confirmation relative to earlier interface-growth experiments.
Whether other members see a statistical-physics prize as sufficiently distinct from the 2021 complex-systems and 2024 neural-network prizes.
How much weight colleagues give to universality and conceptual reach compared with a clear instrument or technological payoff.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile: none of my frequent co-authors is among the credited names for any shortlisted candidate. My work on random-matrix theory is scientifically close to the exact KPZ solutions, but that is intellectual proximity, not a personal or institutional tie. I share a Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson (Chalmers), which could matter for B017, which Johansson ranks first, but I have no known collaboration with that community.
